text: {"findings":[{"rule":"K2","where":"ClaimIssuer.isClaimValid / getRecoveredAddress / revokeClaim (revocation keyed by raw signature bytes)","severity":"HIGH","why":"Revocation stores the exact signature bytes, but getRecoveredAddress uses ecrecover without rejecting high-s or alternate-v signatures. The holder can submit a malleated version of the same signature, which recovers to the same signer but is not in revokedClaims. The holder's own identity key can then re-add it, so a revoked wallet becomes verified again and can receive tokens.","steps":"1) Issuer calls revokeClaim for idB's original claim, which stores that signature as revoked. 2) b takes the original (r,s,v) and builds (r, n-s, v^1) with v flipped between 27 and 28. 3) b calls idB.addClaim(KYC_TOPIC, 1, claimIssuer, malleatedSig, data, \"\"), which passes isClaimValid. 4) ir.isVerified(b) is true again, so token.transfer or mint to b succeeds."}]}
